cases.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
learning_objectives: Compare multiple deterministic mechanism tracks without treating them as treatment recommendations.
Distinguish gene–disease association strength from intervention direction.
Recognize population-constraint warnings, capped evidence, and therapeutic precedent.
cases.debrief: Similar association strength can coexist with different mechanisms, safety context, evidence completeness, and translational precedent.

cases.title: Huntington disease
learning_objectives: Understand why ordinary small-variant counts can miss repeat-expansion biology.
cases.debrief: An insufficient-data heuristic is not a negative statement about an established disease gene.

cases.title: Spinal muscular atrophy
learning_objectives: Distinguish SMN1 disease biology from SMN2 splice modulation and known ASO precedent.
cases.debrief: Splice modulation can change productive transcript output without being the opposite of every knockdown strategy.

cases.title: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
learning_objectives: Separate gene-level direction from exon skipping, reading-frame restoration, and sequence design.
cases.debrief: Target prioritization and sequence or exon design are separate scientific problems.

cases.title: Hereditary ATTR amyloidosis
learning_objectives: Connect toxic protein reduction, tissue delivery, and indication-specific therapeutic precedent.
cases.debrief: Therapeutic precedent is informative context, not proof that every intervention or disease context is equivalent.

cases.title: Dravet syndrome
learning_objectives: Recognize haploinsufficiency and why non-selective knockdown logic can be hazardous.
cases.debrief: Association strength cannot choose intervention direction, and restoration-oriented logic still requires feasibility and safety review.
